root.label: const and volatile
root.note: Each cv-qualifier applies to one level of a type; the level decides what it protects.

children.label: Levels
children.note: Top-level qualifies the object itself; low-level qualifies what it points to.

children.label: Read right to left
children.note: int const* const p is a const pointer to const int.

children.label: Parameters drop top-level
children.note: void f(int) and void f(const int) declare the same function.

children.label: Prvalues drop cv
children.note: A non-class prvalue is never cv-qualified, so returning const int returns int.

children.label: Arrays and references
children.note: cv on an array applies to its elements; cv on a reference or function type is ignored.

children.label: Qualification conversion
children.note: Adds cv below the top level of a pointer type.

children.label: T** to const T**
children.note: Banned: the writable middle pointer could be made to point at a const object.

children.label: const T* const*
children.note: Allowed: if a level gains const, every level above it except the top must be const.

children.label: Unknown bounds (C++20)
children.note: P0388 lets int(*)[3] convert to const int(*)[].

children.label: Const objects
children.note: Objects created const, or non-mutable subobjects of them.

children.label: Modification is UB
children.note: Writing a const object is undefined, whatever path or cast reaches it.

children.label: Path is irrelevant
children.note: A non-const object reached through const T& may be written after const_cast.

children.label: Under construction
children.note: Const semantics start when the constructor finishes and stop when the destructor starts.

children.label: const member functions
children.note: this has type const X*, so members are accessed as const.

children.label: Shallow const
children.note: Pointer members become T* const; the pointees stay modifiable.

children.label: mutable
children.note: Lets a member change in a const object; not allowed on references, statics or const members.

children.label: Logical const
children.note: Observable state is unchanged even when caches or mutexes change.

children.label: Thread safety
children.note: Callers assume concurrent const calls are safe, so a mutable cache needs a lock or atomic.

children.label: volatile
children.note: Accesses through volatile glvalues are observable behavior.

children.label: Not atomic
children.note: Unsynchronized volatile accesses from two threads are a data race; use std::atomic.

children.label: C++20 deprecations
children.note: ++ and --, using a volatile assignment's value, volatile parameters, returns and bindings.

children.label: Compound assignment
children.note: Deprecated by P1152, then restored by P2327 and CWG 2654; not deprecated in C++23.

children.label: constexpr vs const
children.note: const forbids modification; constexpr also demands constant initialization.

children.label: Top-level only
children.note: constexpr int* p is int* const; the pointee is still writable.

children.label: Integral shortcut
children.note: A const integral variable with a constant initializer is usable in constant expressions.

children.label: Not for doubles
children.note: const double d = 1.0 cannot initialize a constexpr double.

children.label: Members (C++14)
children.note: A constexpr member function is no longer implicitly const.
